parsedVerdict.reasoning: This file is declared as application-layer code, but it defines the HTTP request body contract. The doc comment on CancelOrderBodyDto calls it "The transport contract for POST /orders/:id/cancel". It also uses the class-validator `@IsString()` decorator to validate the incoming request at the framework level. Both of these are transport concerns, which belong to the presentation/infrastructure layer (orders.controller.ts already imports this file). CancelOrderDto, the application command input, is built by extending the HTTP body class, and its comment says the controller merges in the path id. So the application input is shaped around the route instead of standing on its own. Defining an input DTO is a fine job for the application layer. Defining an HTTP body schema with framework validation is not. Confidence is moderate because many NestJS projects deliberately put validated DTOs in the application layer.
